scheme_name: Horticulture Mission for North Eastern Hill Scheme- Meghalaya
description:
The Horticulture Mission for North Eastern Hill Region Scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to promote horticulture in the northeastern states of India. 

This scheme was launched in 2001 as part of the National Horticulture Mission. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to enhance horticultural production in the northeastern hill region, which includes states like Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, and Sikkim. 

The mission aims to increase the area under horticulture crops by 20 percent and to enhance the productivity of horticultural crops by 30 percent by the year 2025. 

The scheme also seeks to improve the income of farmers engaged in horticultural activities by providing them with better access to technology, markets, and financial assistance. 

Under this mission, the government provides financial assistance for the cultivation of various horticultural crops such as fruits, vegetables, spices, and flowers. 

Farmers can receive up to 50 percent of the cost of inputs for horticultural development. 

For specific crops like fruits and vegetables, the assistance can go up to 75 percent for small and marginal farmers. 

The scheme also includes support for the establishment of nurseries, post-harvest management, and marketing of horticultural produce. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is subject to a maximum limit of INR 1 lakh per hectare for fruit crops and INR 50,000 per hectare for vegetable crops. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a resident of the northeastern states, having a minimum age of 18 years, and being engaged in horticultural farming. 

Farmers must also possess land ownership or leasehold rights for the land they intend to cultivate. 

The application process for the Horticulture Mission for North Eastern Hill Region Scheme involves several steps. 

First, interested farmers must approach the local horticulture department office in their respective districts. 

They need to fill out an application form that can be obtained from the office or downloaded from the official website of the Department of Horticulture. 

The application must include details such as the type of crops to be cultivated, the area of land, and the estimated cost of cultivation. 

Farmers are required to submit supporting documents, including proof of land ownership, identity proof, and a bank account statement. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the district horticulture officer. 

The officer will conduct a field visit to verify the details provided in the application. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly into the farmer's bank account. 

The disbursement is typically made in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The scheme also emphasizes capacity building and training for farmers. 

Regular training programs are conducted to educate farmers about modern horticultural practices, pest management, and post-harvest technology. 

The timeline for the implementation of the scheme is ongoing, with no specific end date. 

However, the government reviews the progress of the scheme annually to assess its impact and make necessary adjustments. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Horticulture under the Government of Meghalaya. 

The department is responsible for coordinating with various stakeholders, including farmers, agricultural universities, and research institutions. 

Farmers can contact the Department of Horticulture in Meghalaya at the following address: Directorate of Horticulture, Government of Meghalaya, Shillong. 

The contact number for inquiries is +91-364-222-1234. 

The scheme has shown promising results since its inception. 

According to reports, the area under horticulture in Meghalaya has increased significantly, with a rise of over 30 percent in the last five years. 

The productivity of major horticultural crops has also improved, with an increase of approximately 25 percent in yields. 

The government has also established several farmer producer organizations to facilitate better marketing of horticultural produce. 

These organizations help farmers get better prices for their products by reducing the number of intermediaries in the supply chain. 

The scheme has also contributed to the overall economic development of the region by creating employment opportunities in the horticulture sector. 

It is estimated that the horticulture sector in Meghalaya has the potential to generate over 1 lakh jobs in the coming years. 

The government is also promoting organic farming practices under this scheme to enhance the quality of horticultural produce. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt organic methods of cultivation to meet the growing demand for organic products in both domestic and international markets. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme provides support for the establishment of cold storage facilities to reduce post-harvest losses. 

Cold storage facilities are crucial for preserving the quality of perishable horticultural produce. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 200 crores for the implementation of this scheme in Meghalaya for the financial year 2023-2024. 

This budget will be utilized for various activities, including providing financial assistance to farmers, conducting training programs, and establishing infrastructure. 

The Horticulture Mission for North Eastern Hill Region Scheme is a vital initiative that aims to transform the horticulture landscape of Meghalaya and other northeastern states. 

By focusing on enhancing production, improving income, and promoting sustainable practices, the scheme is poised to make a significant impact on the livelihoods of farmers in the region. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme and is committed to providing the necessary support to ensure its success. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to improve their agricultural practices and enhance their economic well-being. 

The Horticulture Mission for North Eastern Hill Region Scheme exemplifies the government's efforts to promote sustainable agriculture and improve the quality of life for farmers in Meghalaya. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a vibrant horticulture sector that contributes to the overall development of the northeastern region of India.
